summary: RFC 6514 created a space of Tunnel Type code points for the BGP PMSI Tunnel attribute but no IANA registry for it. This document updates RFC 6514 to create that registry so further values can be allocated.

eli5.summary: Numbers were handed out with no official list. This RFC creates the official list so new numbers for multicast tunnel types can be recorded.

questions: bgp pmsi tunnel attribute code points
how are bgp tunnel type code points allocated
subtitle: Register and allocate code points for BGP multicast tunnel types

tldr.problem: RFC 6514 defined a space of tunnel type code points for the BGP PMSI Tunnel attribute but did not create an IANA registry for allocating new values.
tldr.mechanism: An IANA registry named P-Multicast Service Interface Tunnel (PMSI Tunnel) Tunnel Types is created with allocation policies: values 0x00-0xFA use IETF Review, 0xFB-0xFE are experimental, and 0xFF is reserved.
tldr.outcome: New PMSI tunnel types (like the Inter-Area P2MP Segmented LSPs) can be allocated from the official registry, ensuring no conflicts and clear documentation.

today: RFC 7385 creates the IANA registry for PMSI tunnel type code points, completing the work started by RFC 6514. It was updated by RFC 8317 and RFC 8338.

sections.title: The Missing Registry
sections.content:
RFC 6514 introduced the BGP P-Multicast Service Interface Tunnel (PMSI Tunnel) attribute, which uses an 8-bit Tunnel Type field to specify the type of multicast tunnel (RSVP-TE P2MP, mLDP P2MP, PIM-SSM, and others). RFC 6514 assigned the values 0-7 but did not create an IANA registry.

As new tunnel types were needed—particularly for Inter-Area P2MP Segmented LSPs—there was no official way to allocate code points or document them.
sections.eli5: The old document gave out the first few numbers but never set up an official place to record new ones.

sections.title: The Registry
sections.content:
A new IANA registry is created in the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) Parameters registry, named "P-Multicast Service Interface Tunnel (PMSI Tunnel) Tunnel Types". The initial values (0x00-0x07) from RFC 6514 are included.

Allocation policy: values 0x00 to 0xFA use IETF Review (allocation by standards action), values 0xFB to 0xFE are experimental and not assigned, and 0xFF is reserved. Only 0xFF can change its status through Standards Action.
sections.eli5: The official list starts with the types from the old document. New ones follow a clear process. Some numbers are saved for experiments.

sections.title: Tunnel Types
sections.content: The initial registry includes: no tunnel information present, RSVP-TE P2MP LSP, mLDP P2MP LSP, PIM-SSM Tree, PIM-SM Tree, BIDIR-PIM Tree, Ingress Replication, and mLDP MP2MP LSP (from RFC 6514). Values 0x08 to 0xFA are unassigned and available for allocation.
sections.eli5: The list covers the main tunnel types already defined and leaves room for future ones.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: RFC 7385 creates the registry that was missing from RFC 6514. The registry enables standardized allocation of new tunnel type code points. It was updated by RFC 8317 and RFC 8338.
sections.eli5: Now there is an official place to record new tunnel types as they are needed.
